FATA (Member, IEEE) received the bachelor’s degree in computer engineering and the master’s degree in electrical engineering from Manhattan University, in 2024 and 2025, respectively. He is currently with PepsiCo, Valhalla, NY, as a Research and Development Engineer. He has received two summer internships during his time of study. The first internship was an Electrical Engineering Intern with Central Hudson, in Summer 2023, and another internship as a Research and Development Engineer with the Global Equipment Development Department, PepsiCo. His research interests include assistive technologies for the visually impaired, neural networks, RF devices, and efficient analog and digital hardware design. He was inducted into numerous honors societies during his time of study, including Tau Beta Pi and Epsilon Sigma Pi. He was inducted into Tau Beta Pi as a Junior which required him to be within the top 12.5% of the Engineering Class. He was inducted into Epsilon Sigma Pi as a Senior, which is the highest scholastic honor that can be earned at Manhattan University. Additionally, he was elected Next in Merit for the Computer Engineering Medal, in 2024. WAFA M. ELMANNAI (Member, IEEE) is currently an Associate Professor of electrical and computer engineering at Manhattan University. She is the Founder and Co-Director of the Women’s Research Mentorship Program at Manhattan University, established through the Women and Gender Resource Center and supported by a 2023–2024 AAUW Community Action Grant. This initiative promotes research engagement among undergraduates through mentorship and academic exploration. Her research interests include the intersection of emerging technologies and inclusive computing, encompassing assistive technologies, smart systems, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things (IoT), mobile computing, computer architecture, and quantum cryptography. Dr. Elmannai is a UDL Teaching Fellow. She is an Active Member of several professional and honor societies, including IEEE, the IEEE Communications Society, Eta Kappa Nu, Phi Kappa Phi, UPE, SWE, and the Arab American Association of Engineers and Architects (AAAEA). She has published extensively in respected national and international venues and has served in various professional roles, including several IEEE conferences, the International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing Conference, and American Society for Engineering Education (ASEE). She has contributed to the peer-review process and the development of high-quality technical programs in areas, such as artificial intelligence and smart systems. She was a recipient of the AAUW International Fellowship. She has supervised and co-supervised numerous undergraduate and graduate research projects. She served during her graduate studies as the Chapter President and the Vice President of the Upsilon Pi Epsilon (UPE) Honor Society, the UB AAUW Ambassador, and the Vice President of the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) at UB. She now continues this leadership as the IEEE-HKN Chapter Advisor at Manhattan University.
